statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 5% (low), Stress 38% (moderate), Confidence 85% (high). The venue is halted for every hour of the published horizon.
recommendation: Tail rests at a closed-market floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. No danger window is published, because no venue quotes at any point in this horizon and there is therefore no evidence-based interval to flag. The material forward checkpoints fall outside the window: the Sunday 22:00 UTC futures reopen, where accumulated US-Iran developments and any shift in September Fed pricing would be expressed as a single gap rather than as an observable path, and the US Labor Day holiday on Monday 7 September, which delays the first full US cash session to 8 September. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state, and subsequent assessment cycles will score the reopen once a live price path exists.
headline: Nasdaq-100 finished the payroll week at 29,544.15 after an orderly two-way session; with CME futures settled since Friday 21:00 UTC the entire 24-hour horizon is a halted venue and Tail sits at a closed-market floor
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed Friday's August payroll session at 29,544.15, up 0.21% from a 29,482.32 prior close, having opened at 29,539.57, extended to 29,655.22, fully retraced that advance to a 29,440.15 low and recovered into the cash close. Retracement occurred repeatedly in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure that the Tail score measures. CME equity index futures settled at 21:00 UTC on Friday, so no live price path exists for NQ futures or the NAS100 CFD at this assessment, and none will exist until the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen roughly twenty-two hours after the final published hour. Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday, so the first full US cash session follows on 8 September. The index outperformed a weaker tape: the S&P 500 fell about 0.38% to 7,718.60, the Dow about 0.51% and the Nasdaq Composite 0.29% to 26,506.99, while the tracked semiconductor complex was uniformly higher, led by Micron up 6.10%, AMD up 4.69% and Intel up 4.51%, against five of eight megacaps lower including Tesla down 5.92%, Apple down 2.51% and Microsoft down 2.04%. That dispersion is a rotation signature rather than the aligned single-direction stack that would justify a raised Tail. Volatility confirmed the orderly reading, with VIX closing at 14.53, up 1.47%, inside a 13.80-14.58 range. The August employment report, verified at the BLS, printed 162,000 nonfarm payrolls against roughly 53,000 expected, with 55,000 of upward revisions across June and July, unemployment steady at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% over the year. Rate transmission stayed contained rather than disorderly: the H.15 release still shows 3 September as its latest official column, at 4.34% for the 2-year and 4.77% for the 10-year, and September hike pricing ended the week near 58% on CME FedWatch against 49.4% a day earlier, ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC. The Federal Reserve communications blackout for that meeting runs from Saturday 5 September to Thursday 17 September and begins at 00:00 Eastern inside this horizon, which removes official commentary as a weekend catalyst. Energy remains the live geopolitical channel: WTI settled at $91.48, up 0.20%, and Brent at $92.68, up 0.8%, for weekly gains of nearly 10% and 7.6%, the steepest since mid-July, as US-Iran hostilities resumed in the seventh month of the conflict, with four Hormuz transits reported Thursday against a ten-day average near fifteen and US diesel at a record $5.85 per gallon. Delayed shared cross-asset context, used only as supporting evidence and never as live price-path evidence, showed the same dispersion rather than one-way index structure, with latest-session NQ marginally positive against weaker ES and YM and semiconductor industry groups strongly higher. With the venue halted for the entire horizon, Tail is published at a closed-market floor of 5%, while Stress at 38% represents unpriced weekend exposure to active Middle East escalation and a firmer September rate path rather than any observed drawdown.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours span the calm pre-payroll regime, the August employment release, its decay into the Friday cash close and the first hours of the weekend halt. Tail sat at 12-13% through the Asian hours and drifted to 17% into the European session while Stress climbed steadily from 51% to 62% ahead of the print. The 12:00 UTC hour carried the only genuine spike, with Tail at 24%, Stress at 76% and Confidence down to 74% as event/whipsaw conditions took over on the 162,000 payroll surprise. Price discovery then proved orderly: the initial move was retraced, Tail fell to 20% and 18% over the following two hours and back into the low teens through the US afternoon, with dominant mode moving from event/whipsaw to mixed as semiconductor strength offset megacap weakness. The final three hours step down to a 5% closed-market floor with Stress at 38% once futures settled at 21:00 UTC. The published series remained EA_ON and green for 22 of the 24 hours, with WATCH and yellow only in the two hours immediately around the release.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the weekend halt. CME equity index futures settled at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday 6 September, roughly twenty-two hours after this horizon ends, and Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday. Because no venue quotes during any published hour, the pathological price path that Tail measures cannot form, so forecast Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-market floor and the dominant mode of normal denotes a halted rather than a directional regime. Stress starts at 38% and drifts to 44% through Saturday to reflect weekend information accumulating unpriced against active US-Iran hostilities and a firmer September rate path; that exposure is real for anything carried through the break but is expressed as a single reopen gap rather than as a tradable path. The Federal Reserve communications blackout ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC begins at 00:00 Eastern on 5 September, inside the horizon, freezing the official rate-path channel for the remainder of the window and leaving geopolitical reporting as the only live weekend catalyst. Confidence decays from 85% to 74% purely with distance from the verified Friday evidence cutoff, since coverage itself is complete and was reverified this cycle. No macro release falls inside the horizon; the next verified checkpoints are the 8 September NY Fed inflation expectations and 3-year auction, PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC.
